corpus_note: Task 309's labelled real-change corpus. Every scenario is an UPSTREAM commit in a repo already pinned by scripts/cross_repo_samples.json (R6.3's qualifying corpus). Nothing here is authored: the change and its tests were written by that project's maintainers, so the labels are ground truth independent of code-atlas. scripts/test_impact_recall.py re-derives every path list from git and refuses a scenario whose committed labels no longer match the commit.

ground_truth.collection_method: upstream co-change: for commit HEAD, the production files are the modified non-test source files of the sample's language and the expected test files are the modified test-directory source files of the same commit
ground_truth.independent_of: code-atlas — the labels are the upstream authors' own edits, not a graph query
ground_truth.why_not_exhaustive: a commit's authors touch the tests they judged necessary, never every test that exercises the change, so an unlabelled test file is not evidence of a false positive — precision is therefore not computed (309 scope item 3)
ground_truth.verification: each commit's diff was read and kept only where the test edit demonstrably exercises the production edit; the per-scenario hand_verification field records that reading

selection_rule: walking each sample's history back from its pinned sha, take commits that MODIFY at least one non-test and at least one test source file of the sample's language, with at most 4 production and at most 3 test files, in reverse-chronological order, keeping the first that survive hand verification. Every rejection is recorded below so the order cannot be cherry-picked silently.

rejected.reason: the only non-test file it modifies is root-level random-tests.php, a manual fuzz script, not production source
